normalize, validate, hash, and write staging

CAS activation record while holding lease
no write, sequence increment, or duplicate event

acquire admission and install intent fingerprint slot
acquire record exact revision without current
CAS claim CREATING(N) as owner N + 1
return resident or use exact resume path

Events reduce latency but are not the source of truth.
acquireCurrent atomically pins one AVAILABLE revision.
Publish activation holds a BundleLease through current CAS.
The Session owns a TemplateLease to that exact entry.
A committed CREATING record pins its original revision.
Retry requires the same fingerprint and a newer owner generation.
Delete, eviction, and resume compete through one lifecycle slot.
Only completed content blocks are durable.
Resume never falls back to current.
Dynamic authorization never comes from the Template.
Upstream, UI uses a separate public WebSocket scoped by chat_id.
mate-service resolves the authoritative chat_id to session_id mapping.
chat_id never enters this internal Runtime flow.
The public and internal hops independently own HTTP 101, connection ID,
request ID, event sequence, Ping/Pong, backpressure, and close state.
mate-service rebuilds semantic Frames; it is not a byte tunnel.
The gateway validates trusted session-affinity metadata before HTTP 101.
The metadata is server-derived and is not an authorization or owner token.
There is no Redis owner, cross-Pod forwarding, or distributed active-Run lease.
Pod restart or affinity-target loss cannot continue a Run across Pods.
